valuation.method: Forward adjusted EPS x P/E. Each case uses FY2027 adjusted EPS (the year an investor at the 2027-11-18 target date is pricing). Anchors: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $1.99 (vs $1.81), 2026 guidance narrowed to $6.70-6.80 with results expected near the top end, long-term 5-7% adjusted EPS growth through 2030 from a $6.30 2025 base, top half of the range from 2028. FY2027 EPS values are our assumptions off a roughly $6.77 2026 base. Multiples are judgement against regulated-utility forward ranges, not broker targets. US common share in USD, so no ADR or FX conversion applies.

bear.driver: Rate-case outcomes and higher financing costs slow growth to the low end and utility multiples compress

base.driver: Mid-range 5-7% growth from rate-base investment and load growth

bull.driver: Upper-end growth on data-center load and constructive regulation supports a premium multiple

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 EPS of $7.18 the close of $129.16 implies 18.0x (19.1x on 2026 EPS of about $6.77). Named analyst targets were not retrieved; firm-level targets from spring 2026 were $138-143.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $7.18 (5.6% of the close, 5.6 percentage points of price return).
valuation.watch_metric: Adjusted EPS versus the guided $6.70-6.80 for 2026 and the 2027 guidance midpoint relative to the 5-7% growth path.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and full-year 2026 results with 2027 guidance, expected around February 2027 (date not announced).

analyst_notes: No named-analyst calls with verifiable dates were retrieved, so coverage is marked unavailable. Firm-level spring 2026 targets (Barclays $143, BMO $143, Evercore $140, UBS $140, Mizuho $139) predate the Q3 beat and are stale; they imply roughly 19-20x base EPS against our 18.5x.
